name: Anterolateral approach to the distal tibia
corridor: Lateral to tibialis anterior with the anterior-compartment tendons and muscle retracted medially beneath the protected superficial peroneal nerve

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with a bump as needed, free ankle motion, and access for AP, lateral, mortise, and traction imaging.

setup.text: Use CT-based fragment mapping, confirm soft-tissue recovery, coordinate any fibular incision, and plan plate and distractor trajectories before incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark tibial crest, fibula, ankle joint, fourth metatarsal axis, superficial-peroneal-nerve course, and talonavicular joint.

incision.text: Center the incision on the ankle joint, aligned with the fourth metatarsal distally and midway between tibia and fibula proximally; limit proximal extension because anterior-compartment muscles arise from fibula.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness flaps, identify the superficial peroneal nerve where it crosses the incision, mobilize it, and open fascia beneath it.

deep_interval.text: Incise extensor retinaculum and retract the anterior-compartment tendons, including peroneus tertius, medially from syndesmosis, distal-tibial periosteum, and capsule.

layers.text: Skin, superficial-peroneal-nerve plane, anterior-compartment fascia/retinaculum, extensor tendons and muscle, capsule/periosteum, then plafond.

structures_encountered.text: Superficial peroneal nerve, extensor tendons, peroneus tertius, extensor digitorum brevis, anterior syndesmosis, capsule, distal tibia, and talar neck are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Superficial peroneal nerve, deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels medially, extensor tendons, anterior syndesmosis, fracture-fragment blood supply, and talar cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The superficial peroneal nerve predictably crosses the proximal incision; identify it before fascial opening and protect it throughout retraction and closure.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the anterior compartment medially as a unit without excessive pressure on the deep neurovascular bundle or stripping articular fragments.

exposure.text: Provides broad anterior and anterolateral plafond visualization, reaches near the medial malleolus, and supports tibial and fibular fixation beneath robust lateral soft tissue.

limitations.text: Direct medial-joint access and proximal extension are limited by the anterior-compartment origin and neurovascular anatomy.

extensions.text: Extend distally toward talonavicular joint or elevate EDB for talar-neck distractor placement; avoid unnecessary proximal dissection.

indications.text: Use for many complete-articular pilon fractures, anterior/anterolateral partial-articular patterns, and selected extra-articular fractures requiring anterior plating.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose another corridor when the dominant pathology is medial/posteromedial, lateral soft tissues are compromised, or adequate skin bridges cannot be preserved.

implant_implications.text: Supports anterolateral buttress and submuscular bridge plates; place distractor rod posterolaterally so it does not obstruct reduction or implants.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Verify articular reduction, length, alignment, talar centering, plate position, and screw containment on AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views.

closure.text: Repair capsule, retinaculum, and fascia without entrapping superficial peroneal nerve; close only when full-thickness flaps are viable and tension free.

complications.text: Complications include superficial or deep peroneal neuropathy, wound necrosis, infection, extensor adhesions, malreduction, nonunion, stiffness, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: Add a separate medial or posteromedial window when a key fragment cannot be reduced safely through the anterolateral corridor rather than stripping across the plafond.

procedure_applications.condition: Anterior or anterolateral articular injury and lateral metaphyseal comminution require direct reduction and buttress access
An extra-articular distal-tibia fracture is treated with an anterior-compartment submuscular plate
